title: The trail, back on top of the ground and standing for half a minute
question: Is it sitting at the right height now, and is half a minute long enough to walk a colony somewhere?
context_md:
Your two notes, both done: *"Make it last even longer (at least 2x more)"* and *"if it is fully underground, an ant wont smell it either... it should be a little height, just at/slightly above ground versus fully below."*

**You were right that it had gone under, and I had a number saying it hadn't.** He lays at his feet, and a gnome standing on soil is **sunk four cells into it** — that is by design, it is what makes walking through a drift feel like wading. So his feet are under the surface and so was the trail. My check measured *"how far down to the first solid cell"*, which reads zero for a trail lying on the ground **and** zero for one buried inside it. It now reads height as a signed number: the old version measures **4 cells under, all 64 samples buried**; this one **1 cell above, none buried**. Both strips are over soil, not rock — that is the only place the bug exists.

**On lasting longer: no amount of widening or strengthening could do it, so the trail now works differently.** A scent mark laid once can't survive much past 20 seconds whatever shape it is — that limit is set by how fast the world forgets, which is shared with the ants and is not mine to change. I widened it to five times the size as a test: it bought 5 more seconds and nothing more.

So what he lays is now a **standing** instruction, the thing its price always said it was: he pays once by walking the route, and it holds itself up for half a minute, dimming the whole way, then goes. The oldest end fades first, so the trail retreats toward him rather than vanishing all at once — at 28s the half nearest him is still there and the far half has gone.

Both strips step **0 / 10 / 20 / 28 seconds** after he stops laying. Same walk, same ground, same seed.

items.caption: laid at his feet — which on soil is under it

items.label: now
items.caption: laid on the ground surface, and held up for 30s
